solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pests concealed in recess mostly

indicators.note: in places the word for concealed inside the shortened recess
mostly means all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: an apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church
concealed means hid

explanation.surface: Garden pests are lurking unseen in a nook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the church recess, and 'in' places the concealed word inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking insects that gardeners treat as pests.

clue.text: A European levy to produce inflation?

parts.note: a rate is a local tax or levy

explanation.surface: A Europe-wide tax is proposed as a way to drive up prices.
explanation.walkthrough: Inflation here is filling with air, not rising prices; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a liquid or soil with air is to make it swell with gas, a literal inflation.

clue.text: South American farms in a shed I can let out

indicators.note: let out suggests the letters are released and rearranged freely

explanation.surface: Ranches are found inside a shed one might rent out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' turns A SHED I CAN into the Spanish word for estates.
explanation.definitionFit: Large estates or ranches in Spanish-speaking America are called by this Spanish word.

clue.text: Envoy lacks ultimate qualification

indicators.note: lacks ultimate tells us the final letter of the envoy word is dropped

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat

explanation.surface: An ambassador is missing the final certificate he needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks ultimate' drops the T from DIPLOMAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate awarded for completing a course of study is a formal qualification.

clue.text: People photographing fish

definitions.meaning: people taking quick photographs, as in snapping a picture
a family of sea fish prized for eating, such as the red species

explanation.surface: Photographers are at work on a catch of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual photographers snap pictures; the same word names a group of sea fish.

clue.text: Singer in London square hailing gent rudely

indicators.note: rudely signals the letters are roughly handled into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer in a London square is rudely greeting a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudely' rearranges HAILING GENT; the definition alludes to the song about a bird singing in Berkeley Square, a fashionable London square.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous song has this songbird singing in Berkeley Square in Mayfair.

clue.text: Sage perhaps makes fuss over book

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the fuss word above the book letter

parts.note: pother is an old word for commotion or fuss

explanation.surface: Someone is making a fuss over a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sage' looks like a wise person, but it is the herb; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is one example of a leafy plant grown for flavouring in cooking.

clue.text: Praise old group given a boost

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: given a boost means raised up, so in a down entry the word is written upwards

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: Former band members get applause as their career is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a boost' lifts LOT, which in a down entry reads TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud or speak highly of someone is to praise them.

clue.text: Sing to a duke in comfortable surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the comfortable word goes around the other letters

parts.note: serene means calm and at ease, comfortable

explanation.surface: A duke is serenaded in a cosy setting.
explanation.walkthrough: A and D go inside SERENE.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform a love song beneath someone's window is to sing to them.

clue.text: Cook's instruction ready to embrace Eastern cuisine's starter

indicators.note: to embrace means the ready word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: fruit that is ripe is ready to eat

indicators.note: starter means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A chef is told to have an Asian dish's first course prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course; it gives just the C of cuisine's.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of directions for preparing a dish is what a cook follows.

clue.text: Troublemaker a soldier has to turn endlessly back

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: back means the shortened word is read in reverse
endlessly drops the final letter of the word for turn

parts.note: to rotate is to turn

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to keep spinning round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ROTATE to ROTAT, and 'back' reverses it to TATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble-rouser who stirs up unrest is a troublemaker.

clue.text: Piece following article on hot part of Aga saga

indicators.note: following places the piece word after the others

parts.note: the is the definite article
an Aga is a British cast-iron range cooker, and the hob is its hot top
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Next to the article comes a passage about a stove's hotplate in an Aga family saga.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a cast-iron range cooker found in British country kitchens; 'Aga saga' is a genre of cosy middle-class novel, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's long adventure tale of Bilbo's journey is an example of a saga.

clue.text: Monk well read in Latin keeps order at home

indicators.note: keeps means the Latin word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: bene is the Latin word for well
an edict is an official order
in means at home

explanation.surface: A scholarly monk, fluent in Latin, keeps discipline in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well read' looks like learned; it means 'well' read as Latin, BENE, which holds EDICT and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the order founded by St Benedict is a monk.

clue.text: French girl's name? No, English one

parts.note: elle is French for she, standing for a girl

explanation.surface: Is it a French girl's name? No, it is an English one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a French name, but ELLE is only the French word for she; adding N for name gives an English girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female forename used in England, so it is an English girl's name.

clue.text: Getting exhausted managers a place to dry out

parts.note: draining means emptying or exhausting
a board is a group of managers or directors

explanation.surface: Tired executives need somewhere to recover from drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry out' suggests sobering up; it is where washed dishes drain beside a sink.
explanation.definitionFit: The ridged surface beside a kitchen sink is where washed crockery is left to drip dry.

clue.text: Piece of kit I can reorder with electronics company around

indicators.note: around means the company name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Apple is the computer and electronics company

indicators.note: reorder tells us to rearrange the letters given

explanation.surface: A gadget can be reordered from a tech firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorder' shuffles I CAN, and 'around' wraps the tech firm's name about the result; 'Piece of kit' suggests a uniform item but means a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or machine, such as a washer, is an item of equipment, a piece of kit.

clue.text: With the team depleted, Kent lose badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Kent, a county cricket side, play with a weakened team and lose heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is an English county with a cricket side. 'badly' rearranges KENT LOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A minimal staff or crew, kept to the bare bones, describes a depleted team.

clue.text: Smack accompanied by slap then settle one's differences

parts.note: a smack is a loud kiss
and means together with, accompanied by
slap is theatre slang for cosmetics, make-up

explanation.surface: A row of blows is followed by a reconciliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' and 'slap' look like blows; one is a kiss, the other face paint.
explanation.definitionFit: To end a quarrel and become friendly again is to settle one's differences.

clue.text: Chemical giving one very good mood

parts.note: an ace is one, as on a playing card, and also means very good
tone is mood or feeling

explanation.surface: A substance is said to give a fine feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A colourless solvent, used in nail varnish remover, is an organic chemical.

clue.text: Giving investiture initially in ruined castle

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the jumbled castle
ruined means the castle's letters are knocked about
initially means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An investiture ceremony is staged in a ruined castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives I, and 'ruined' rearranges CASTLE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchy or yielding material gives under pressure, so giving means flexible.

clue.text: Writer Charles perhaps taken in by trick

indicators.note: taken in by means the Charles word goes inside the trick word

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
Ray Charles was the American singer, so Charles is a Ray

explanation.surface: An author called Charles has been duped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author; it is something you write with.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured wax stick used for drawing or writing is a writer in the sense of an instrument.

clue.text: Caught in temptation to make riches

indicators.note: in puts the caught letter inside the temptation word

parts.note: a lure is a temptation or enticement
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is trapped by the lure of getting rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Money, especially gained dishonestly, is filthy wealth.

clue.text: Outer surface about to corrode

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about
to rust is to corrode

explanation.surface: The outside is beginning to rot away.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard outer layer of bread or the earth is its outer surface.

clue.text: Knight put in good spirits engaging against old fighter

indicators.note: engaging means holding the other letters within

parts.note: cheer means good spirits
V, short for versus, means against
Muhammad Ali was a famous boxer of the past

explanation.surface: A knight in a cheerful mood takes on a veteran boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaging' means holding inside; Muhammad Ali, the boxer, is the usual 'old fighter' in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a horseman is used for a member of certain orders of knighthood.

clue.text: After time, European organisation gets pick-me-up from Germany

indicators.note: after places the European group after the time letter

parts.note: the EU is the European Union
a tonic is a pick-me-up

explanation.surface: Eventually a European body receives a boost from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes the Germanic peoples, so it means German in character or origin.

clue.text: Tight pain, variable

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
Y is a mathematical variable

explanation.surface: A tight sensation of pain varies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' looks like taut; it means mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tight with money is being miserly, the same as mean.

clue.text: Did gas develop net trade?

indicators.note: develop means the letters evolve into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A question of whether gas supply boosted overall trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' looks like fuel; here it means to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is to chat idly, so did gas means chatted.

clue.text: Show on television loose material that's new

parts.note: scree is loose stones on a mountain slope

explanation.surface: Broadcasting some fresh loose stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast a programme is to show it on the small screen, a synonym for transmit.
